You may remember Bottomless from episode 124 when we had co-founder and CEO Michael Mayer on the show. I'm also a bottomless customer and like the service and idea so much I became an investor.

thesis: This episode argues that Facebook (META) faces significant headwinds due to flat U.S. user growth and a product perceived as ad-heavy rather than social, creating challenges in shifting users to new products. In contrast, it highlights Pinduoduo as a rare mobile-native commerce success story that achieved massive scale and rapid growth, while noting Snapchat's smaller user base relative to Facebook and Instagram's high valuation.

claims.claim: Facebook faces challenges in shifting users to new products because its feed is on autopilot and generating massive revenue, while user growth in the U.S. has been flat for almost a decade.
claims.quote: So I think Facebook runs into the challenge of, okay, we're trying to shift people into stories. We're trying to shift people into the marketplace. We're trying to get people to use Messenger and build this we chat like ecosystem within our messaging product. But our feed makes so much money. It's on autopilot right now.

claims.claim: Facebook's user growth in the U.S., where most revenue comes from, has been flat for almost a decade, growing only one or two percent a quarter since its IPO.
claims.quote: And I think we've kind of seen sort of with Facebook, if you look at their user growth in the U.S., which is where most of their revenue and cash flow comes from, it's been flat for almost a decade. They're growing like one or two percent a quarter since they IPOed in the U.S.

claims.claim: Users are leaving Facebook because the product is perceived as just ads with no friends, making it a product people do not enjoy using.
claims.quote: Obviously, they've reached a lot of people in the U.S., but a lot of people are turning out because the product, they're just like, I don't want to use this. It's just a bunch of ads and none of my friends are on here anymore. It's just not a product I enjoy using.

claims.claim: Snapchat has about 86 million daily active users in North America, which is about half as much as Facebook and close to Instagram.
claims.quote: So when you really look at the numbers, Snapchat has about 86, 84 million daily active users in North America, which is about half as much as Facebook pretty close to Instagram.

claims.claim: Analysts value Instagram between $200 billion and $400 billion.
claims.quote: And analysts Pegg Instagram is being worth anywhere from $200 to $400 billion. I mean, the number is pretty insane how valuable they think that business is.

claims.claim: Pinduoduo is the first commerce company to hit scale and reach hundreds of millions of people that was built for mobile.
claims.quote: I think PIN Duo Duo Duo, it's the same thing with TikTok and ByteDance. It's the first commerce company that's hit scale and reaches hundreds of millions of people that was built for mobile.

claims.claim: Pinduoduo grew by leveraging WeChat mini programs and reached 100 million users in their WeChat mini program as of 2019.
claims.quote: So a couple of the really big mini programs that really took off were Pindu-Duo Duo, which, as of 2019, had 100 million users in their Wii chat mini program.

claims.claim: Pinduoduo is one of the fastest growing companies ever, with $4.1 billion in revenue in its fifth year.
claims.quote: It's probably one of the fastest growing companies ever. I mean, the revenue year five of a business, I think they did $4.1 billion in U.S. revenue, that might be off a little bit. But it's just insane how fast it grew.

claims.claim: Pinduoduo takes a small cut of transactions, with an average of 0.6% mentioned in their disclosures.
claims.quote: And it's Pinduodoo taking a cut of, I think they said in one of their disclosures, like, 0.6% is the average. That number could also be off. But it's just a really small cut.
